# Archive reach — what the free record can and cannot repair (2026-09-02, session A)

*Source of the dated line in `AUDIT.md`. Kept as its own file because `AUDIT.md` is generated by
`src/spine_audit.py`; a hand-added section there is lost on the next regeneration, this one is not.*

## The finding

**2026-09-02 — 27 post-2000 encyclopaedia-only records, 4 routes consulted each (9 probed in all),
0 replaced by a primary document, 19 with nothing found, 8 places to look, 0 unexplained.**

Every one of the 27 events in the corpus whose only citation is an encyclopaedia and whose date is
2000 or later was put through every primary-document route reachable without a key. Not one could be
replaced by a primary document. This is a measurement of **archive reach**, not of effort, and not of
whether the sources exist: for each record the routes either answered and held nothing, or were out of
coverage for a stated reason. No call was left unexplained.

| outcome | n | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| closed-primary | **0** | a government document with its own date naming the event |
| press_candidate | 8 | a dated article sharing the event's terms — a place for Joe to look, never a repair |
| none_found | 19 | every reachable route answered and held nothing for that date |
| partial | 0 | an archival file at the right time on the right subject |
| blocked-by-declassification | 0 | no route could answer at all |

By decade: 2000s 11 none-found; 2010s 5 none-found; 2020s 8 press candidates and 3 none-found.

## The 108 route calls behind that line (27 records x 4 routes)

| route | answered, no hit | hit | out of coverage | why out of coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FRUS | 0 | 0 | **27** | volumes stop in the early 1990s; every record here is 2000 or later |
| Federal Register | **27** | 0 | 0 | in coverage (1994→) for all 27, and held nothing: these are mostly non-US events |
| UK National Archives | 10 | 0 | **17** | the UK 20-year rule — files from 2006 onward are not open yet |
| GDELT DOC 2.0 | 4 | 8 | **15** | coverage begins 2017 |

Read across: for a non-US event between 2000 and 2016 there is **no free route that can supply a primary
document**. FRUS has ended, the UK files are not open, GDELT has not begun, and the Federal Register only
covers US federal action. That window is the whole of the gap, and it is why the automatic second-source
pass over the 473 post-1987 candidates returned "absent" for 438 of them.

## The 9 routes probed, and their state on 2026-09-02

| route | state | covers | yields |
|---|---|---|---|
| FRUS (history.state.gov) | reachable, keyless, **wired** | 1945 → early 1990s | dated government document |
| Federal Register | reachable, keyless, **wired** | 1994 → | dated rule, notice, presidential document |
| UK National Archives Discovery | reachable, keyless, **wired** | all eras subject to the 20-year release rule | file-level record only, never a document |
| GDELT DOC 2.0 | reachable, keyless, **wired** | 2017 → | dated press article (a candidate, not a source) |
| govinfo (GPO) | reachable, **not wired** | US federal publications | needs an `api.data.gov` key; `DEMO_KEY` has an hourly cap low enough that a run would throttle and read as an absence |
| CIA CREST / FOIA reading room | **not reachable** | 1940s–1990s | every search form returns the landing page; results need JavaScript |
| UN Security Council / UN Digital Library | **not reachable** | all | HTTP 403; the digital library serves a JavaScript challenge |
| OPEC archive | **not reachable** | 1960 → | HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) |
| US NARA catalog | **not reachable** | all | the API path returns the JavaScript app shell |

Full table with endpoints: `data/candidates/ROUTE_TABLE.md`. Rules governing what each outcome is allowed
to mean: `data/candidates/DOSSIER_RULE.md` §6.1–§6.6. Per-record dossiers: `data/candidates/repairs/`,
index `data/candidates/repairs_index_sessionA_post2000.json`. Regenerate with
`python3 src/source_repair.py --cohort encyclopaedia --from 2000-01-01 --index-tag sessionA_post2000`.

## What this does not say

It does not say these 27 events are unsourced in history; it says no **keyless, scriptable** route holds a
primary document for them today. A reader with a library subscription, a NARA key, or a FOIA request may
find one. It also does not say the 8 press candidates are wrong — only that keyword overlap cannot
establish that an article is about a particular event, so a human has to look (§6.5).
